paragraphs.text: Chapter 3. Dr. Roylot and Stoke Moran.
What do you think of this case, Watson?
It seems to be very mysterious, I said.
Jips is whistles in the night and the sound of metal.
Perhaps Dr. Roylot doesn't want his step-daughters to marry,
because he doesn't want to give them the money.
And that's why I want to go to Stoke Moran today.
Cried Holmes as the door suddenly opened and a big man appeared.
He was tall and had an angry face.
I am Dr. Grimes B. Roylot of Stoke Moran.
It's a bit calm for April.
And but I hear that the flowers are growing.
You think you're a great detective, but you only make trouble.
When you go out, please close the door because it's getting cold in this room.
I know Miss Stoner was here.
He said, and he left the room quickly.
I only hope he won't hurt Miss Stoner.
I'm going to the records office to get some help with this case.
Holmes came back at two o'clock.
He was holding a piece of paper full of notes and numbers.
I saw the will of Dr. Royal on his wife and studied it carefully.
If the sisters marry, they receive most of the doctors' money.
He certainly has a good reason to want to stop them marrying.
And now, Watson, we must leave for Stoke Moran immediately.
Bring your gun and your toothbrush.
We caught the train for Leatherhead and then took a carriage to Stoke Moran.
Miss Stoner was waiting for us.
I'm very happy to see you.
Dr. Royal Ot went to London and won't be back until late this evening.
We already met the doctor this morning.
He followed me to your house.
But we said nothing of your visit.
What will he say when he returns home?
Tonight, you must lock yourself in your room.
Now, please take me to see the bedrooms.
Holmes looked at the outside of the old house.
Then he looked at the three bedrooms.
Is this your room, Miss Stoner?
I don't think it needs any work.
No, but for some reason my stepfather said,
From now on you must sleep in your sister's room.
The door and window of your rooms are locked at night, aren't they?
We went into Julia's small bedroom.
And Holmes sat down in the corner of the room and looked all around.
He asked, pointing to a bell rope.
The rope hung down near the bed.
It goes to the servants room.
It seems newer than the other things here.
It was put there two years ago.
Because there isn't usually a servant in the house.
Then she didn't need a bell.
Why, this isn't a real bell.
It is fixed to the wall just above the ventilator.
The bell rope and the ventilator were put in at about the same time.
We went to the doctor's room.
There was a round table, a chair, and a big metal chest against the wall.
He asked, pointing to the chest.
There's a small bowl of milk on top of the chest.
Now, let's return to the garden.
